correctness.rationale: For every orbit of every p-ACB operator, applying the hypothesis to each tail T^k x yields \(S_{k+1}\le(K(n-k+1)-1)a_k\). Exact telescoping gives \(a_n\le B_n(K)a_0\), including zero terms. The positive weighted backward shift with \(w_1^p=2K-1\) and \(w_j^p=(K(j+1)-1)/(Kj)\) satisfies a full prefix average K at each basis vector e_j (j≥1), all shorter prefix means ≤K by monotone orbit norms, and all longer means ≤K by truncation; Tonelli transfers the bound to arbitrary ℓp vectors. Taking e1 at horizon2 gives optimal constant K. Decreasing weights give \(\|W^n\|^p=\prod_{r\le n}w_r^p=B_n(K)\) simultaneously. Gamma recurrence and quotient asymptotics are standard; rational exact checks ran through n=11. No finite test is used as proof.

value.rationale: Universal optimal finite-time amplification for every n and every Banach space is a meaningful quantitative invariant of Cesàro stability, needed to predict finite-horizon transient growth. A single explicit positive shift saturates all horizons, giving exact constants and a sharp Gamma leading coefficient. Existing estimates only established the exponent and specific operator profiles; this is not a small isolated numerical refinement or an arbitrary parameter slice. The result also handles the K=1 contraction boundary uniformly.
